newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bourses propose option-related margin trade.
newsitem.headline: Japan bourses propose option-related margin trade.

text.p: The Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) and the Osaka Securities Exchange (OSE) proposed to Japan's Finance Ministry that margin transactions be allowed in individual shares when options on those shares are settled, a ministry source said on Wednesday.

"We have received proposals from the TSE and OSE that margin trades in shares be allowed when options contracts for individual stocks are settled, but we have not received a final request from the bourses and nothing has been decided formally," the source said.
The source added that the use of margin trades would widen the range of instruments available for investors and would help prevent share price manipulation related to option settlements.
MOF was examining the issue of margin trades within the bounds of exisiting regulations, the official said.
A TSE official said that the use of margin trades would help encourage private investors to engage in trading of options on individual shares.
"As soon as MOF grants permission, we plan to discuss it (margin trading) at a board meeting and incorporate it into our regulations concerning options on individual shares," the official said.
Trading in options of individual shares is due to start on July 18.
